title: When Persona Simulations Are Informative: Graph-Structured Signals for Pluralistic Opinion Sensing
abstract: arXiv:2608.22438v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Persona-conditioned large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate survey responses across diverse domains. However, apparent response variation can reflect unconditioned model priors or token sampling noise rather than systematic persona conditioning. We argue that persona-conditioned variation is informative when semantically similar personas exhibit concordant response shifts. To operationalize this principle, we introduce Persona-Conditioned Informativeness (PCI), an unsupervised diagnostic metric that measures whether semantically similar personas deviate in concordant directions relative to item-level sample baselines. By modeling personas as a similarity graph, PCI uses Local Moran's I to quantify local spatial coherence and extract compact persona subsets without using construct labels. translated_title: 当人物模拟具有信息性：基于图结构信号的多元意见感知
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.22438v1 公告类型：新 摘要：人物条件化的大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地被用于模拟跨领域的调查响应。然而，表面上的响应变化可能反映了无条件的模型先验或令牌采样噪声，而非系统性的条件化处理。我们认为，当语义相似的人物表现出一致的响应偏移时，人物条件化的变化才具有信息性。为了操作化这一原则，我们引入了人物条件化信息性（PCI），这是一种无监督的诊断指标，用于衡量语义相似的人物是否相对于项目级样本基线在一致方向上偏离。通过将人物建模为相似性图，PCI利用局部莫兰指数来量化局部空间一致性，并在不使用构造标签的情况下提取紧凑的人物子集。为了在没有外部人类基准的情况下评估PCI，我们测试其使用57个变量恢复既有潜在价值结构的能力。
tldr: 本文提出了一种无监督诊断指标PCI，通过图结构信号衡量人物条件化响应的信息性，以区分系统性条件化与噪声变异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PCI, an unsupervised diagnostic metric using graph-structured signals to assess informativeness of persona-conditioned responses, distinguishing systematic conditioning from noise.
